interviewBank.q: What is CSS and why is it separate from HTML?
interviewBank.answer: CSS is the style language that describes how structured content should be presented. Keeping it separate lets one stylesheet serve many pages, lets the browser cache it, and lets a design change without editing content.

interviewBank.q: What does the cascade actually mean?
interviewBank.answer: When several rules target the same element, the browser resolves them by importance, origin, cascade layers, specificity and source order. The winner supplies each property; it is not a single whole-rule victory.

interviewBank.q: What can CSS not do on its own?
interviewBank.answer: It cannot compute business logic, store data, make network requests or respond to arbitrary input. Those need JavaScript or a server. CSS only reacts to states the browser exposes, such as hover, focus and media conditions.

defenseBank.q: A beginner asks why not put every style inline.
defenseBank.answer: Inline styles cannot be reused, cached or overridden cleanly, and they mix presentation into the content. One external stylesheet keeps the design in a single reviewable place.
steps: Show the same rule repeated on three pages.
Point out the cache and the single edit.

defenseBank.answer: CSS targets structure. Without knowing elements, nesting and attributes there is nothing meaningful to select, and every example becomes unexplained magic.
steps: Show a selector matching a node.

defenseBank.q: How do you explain the presentation layer?
defenseBank.answer: The page is a document with meaning; CSS is the set of decisions about how that meaning is displayed. Changing the decisions does not change the document.
steps: Turn CSS off and show the content.
Turn it on and show the design.
Point out the HTML never changed.

interviewBank.q: Why is an external stylesheet preferred over a style block?
interviewBank.answer: One file can serve every page, the browser caches it across navigation, and the design lives in one reviewable place. A style block is page-specific and has to be repeated.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between file:// and a local server for CSS?
interviewBank.answer: A file URL gives every page an opaque origin and can block modules and fetch, while a local server serves the project over HTTP with the same root-relative behaviour as production.

interviewBank.q: What does the Styles panel show that the source does not?
interviewBank.answer: The live cascade: every rule that matched, which declarations won, which were overridden, and the computed value after inheritance and units are resolved.

defenseBank.q: A learner edits CSS but sees no change.
defenseBank.answer: I check the file is saved, the link path resolves, and the browser is not serving a cached stylesheet before touching the rule.

defenseBank.q: Why not use an absolute file path in href?
defenseBank.answer: It works only on that machine and breaks for every visitor and on every deploy. A relative path travels with the project.

defenseBank.answer: It tells the browser what the linked file is for. Without it the file is just a resource, not a stylesheet to apply.

mcqBank.q: Where does the link element belong?
mcqBank.why: Stylesheet links are metadata and belong in the head.

mcqBank.q: Which file extension does a browser apply as CSS?
mcqBank.why: The server sends .css as text/css and the browser applies it.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between a rule and a declaration?
interviewBank.answer: A rule is a selector plus a declaration block. A declaration is one property-value pair inside that block, ended by a semicolon.

interviewBank.q: What happens when one declaration is invalid?
interviewBank.answer: Only that declaration is dropped. The rest of the rule and the rest of the stylesheet still apply, which is why a typo can look like a completely missing rule.
They start with slash-star and end with star-slash, may span lines, and cannot be nested. The browser removes them before parsing.

defenseBank.q: A learner asks whether the last semicolon is required.
defenseBank.answer: It is optional before a closing brace but I keep it, because inserting another declaration later is the common edit and a missing semicolon then breaks two declarations at once.
steps: Show a rule without the last semicolon.

defenseBank.q: Why insist on one property per line?
defenseBank.answer: Diffs become readable, a missing semicolon is visible, and review comments can point at one line. Minification is the build step’s job.

defenseBank.q: Why does the browser not show a syntax error?
defenseBank.answer: CSS error handling is designed to recover: it drops the bad declaration and continues. DevTools shows the surviving rules, not the ones that were discarded.
steps: Fix it and watch it appear.

mcqBank.q: Which part of a rule chooses the elements?
mcqBank.why: The selector is the part before the braces.

mcqBank.q: Which is valid CSS comment syntax?
mcqBank.why: CSS only supports slash-star block comments.

mcqBank.q: What does a missing closing brace usually cause?
mcqBank.why: The parser keeps reading until it finds a closing brace.

interviewBank.q: Why is external CSS preferred in production?
interviewBank.answer: It is cached once for many pages, keeps content and presentation apart, and allows a whole site to be restyled from one file. Inline and internal styles cannot be shared.

interviewBank.q: Which wins between inline and external CSS?
interviewBank.answer: An inline declaration wins at equal importance because the style attribute is treated as author origin with higher specificity. Only !important in the stylesheet, or a change of importance, overrides it.

interviewBank.q: How do you organise multiple stylesheets?
interviewBank.answer: Load a reset or base layer first, then the design system, then page or component styles, so later files can rely on earlier tokens and win ties deliberately.

defenseBank.q: A learner uses inline styles to fix everything quickly.
defenseBank.answer: It works until the second page needs the same look, or a hover state, or a media query. None of those are expressible inline.
steps: Show the same inline style copied twice.
Add a hover state that inline cannot do.

defenseBank.answer: It breaks the cascade instead of using it, forcing the next fix to be another !important. Specificity and source order should be fixed at the cause.
steps: Show a rule that needed it.

defenseBank.answer: For generated HTML where a single value must be applied, such as an email template or a dynamic brand colour, and for prototyping. It is not a system.
